drug_class: Guanylate cyclase-C agonist (GI motility agent / secretagogue)
purpose: Plecanatide is used to treat chronic idiopathic constipation (constipation with no known cause) and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults. It helps you have more regular, easier bowel movements. It is taken once daily by mouth.
how_it_works: Plecanatide works locally in your intestines — it barely gets absorbed into your bloodstream. It attaches to a specific receptor in the lining of your intestines called guanylate cyclase-C, which causes your intestines to release more fluid into the gut. This extra fluid softens your stool and helps it move through your bowels more easily and more often.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is diarrhea, which can sometimes be severe. You may also notice loose stools, stomach pain, gas, or bloating. If diarrhea becomes severe or you feel dizzy or dehydrated, contact your doctor right away.
warnings: This medication must NEVER be given to children under 6 years old because it can cause severe, life-threatening diarrhea leading to dangerous dehydration. It should also be avoided in children 6 to 18 years old. Tell your doctor if you have a bowel blockage, as this medication should not be used in that case. Keep this medication stored safely away from children at all times.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is one 3 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. If you have trouble swallowing, you can crush the tablet and mix it with applesauce or water. Take it around the same time each day for best results.
